subject.title: openclaw gateway restart hangs on macOS with SMB-mounted volumes (lsof stat() timeout)

question: Should Gateway port checks adopt a layered availability-first design that reserves bounded `lsof` inspection for conflicts, or continue using `lsof` as the primary ownership and health mechanism?
rationale: The observable bug is clear, but the replacement must balance non-blocking health checks against PID ownership, stale-process safety, diagnostics, and consistent behavior across restart, force, and status paths.

options.title: Layer availability and ownership
options.body: Use a non-spawning bounded probe for routine availability, then run time-limited `lsof` only when process identity is actually needed.

options.title: Harden lsof everywhere
options.body: Keep `lsof` as the primary mechanism but batch calls where possible and enforce strict timeouts and consistent failure handling across every caller.

options.title: Wait for stronger live evidence
options.body: Keep the current implementation until the SMB hang is independently reproduced on current main, accepting the reported restart delay in the meantime.

recommendation.title: Layer availability and ownership
recommendation.body: Use a non-spawning bounded probe for routine availability, then run time-limited `lsof` only when process identity is actually needed.

likelyOwner.reason: They were explicitly routed this issue and have recent review context across Gateway restart, stale-process cleanup, and service lifecycle behavior.
